clue.text: In Lancaster, hired clothing

parts.note: John of Gaunt was Duke of Lancaster, so the man known as Lancaster was Gaunt
something hired out is let, as a flat is let

explanation.surface: A costume-hire shop in the Lancashire city of Lancaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lancaster' looks like the city; it is John of Gaunt, the medieval Duke of Lancaster, often simply called Lancaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauntlet is a heavy glove, an item of armour or wear, so it counts as clothing.

clue.text: Race half over, and at last a competitor is coming

indicators.note: turned over means the half-word is read backwards
only the first half of the word race is used, its opening two letters

parts.note: a competitor is a rival

explanation.surface: Halfway through a race, a competitor finally comes into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes RA from RACE and 'over' turns it to AR; 'and at last' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is the act of coming somewhere, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Not a soul to light captive girl's cigarette end

indicators.note: the girl is held captive inside the word for light

parts.note: neon is a kind of light, as in neon signs
Vera is a girl's name

indicators.note: the end of the word cigarette is its last letter

explanation.surface: Nobody will give a light to a captive woman wanting to finish her cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like a verb for lighting a cigarette; it is a noun, a kind of lamp, which takes the girl captive.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means nobody at all, as in 'not a single person'.

clue.text: Get hold of gold vehicle

parts.note: to land something, like a fish or a job, is to get hold of it
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An instruction to seize a golden carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top.

clue.text: Diet might help one to economize

definitions.text: Diet might help one to economize

parts.words: Diet might help one to economize
parts.note: a slimming diet literally lets you pull your waistband in a notch, and the idiom for that means cutting spending

explanation.surface: Advice that going on a diet saves money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to spend less, pictured as pulling a strap in after eating less.

clue.text: Dog finding part of tree said "Gosh!

indicators.note: said tells us the word is heard spoken, giving its sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a bough is a large branch of a tree
wow is an exclamation like gosh

explanation.surface: A dog finds a branch and exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' applies only to the part of the tree: the branch word is replaced by its sound-alike spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Bow-wow is the nursery word for a dog, from its bark.

clue.text: Just out to make three points

parts.note: a make of car or soap is its brand
N, E and W are three compass points: north, east, west

explanation.surface: Something newly released that scores three points.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points are a crossword convention for the letters N, E, S and W.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just out of the shop or factory is new and unused.

clue.text: Document he had twisted

parts.note: a writ is a formal legal document
he'd is the short form of he had

explanation.surface: A man had distorted a document.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist the body about, so writhed is a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Ace flew round doing acrobatics

indicators.note: acrobatics are tumbles and flips, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A flying ace performs loops in an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace' looks like a pilot in the scene; it is the slang adjective meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ace is informal praise meaning excellent or marvellous.

clue.text: Yellow head of crimson bird

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a raven is a large black bird

explanation.surface: A red-headed bird, with yellow a colour clash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' looks like a colour; it means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and craven means lacking courage.

clue.text: Once a Mancunian defender

definitions.meaning: a newspaper formerly titled after Manchester

explanation.surface: A protector who used to come from Manchester.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper was called the Manchester Guardian until 1959, when it dropped the city from its name; a Mancunian is someone or something from Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: The newspaper once bore Manchester's name, and a protector or keeper is someone who defends.

clue.text: Gloomy deliveries by actors

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls delivered
the actors in a play are its cast

explanation.surface: Dismal bowling by a team of actors in a charity match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is dark with cloud, so dull and gloomy.

clue.text: Prince Hamlet initially taken in by one of his people, a girl

indicators.note: the two letters are held inside the word for one of his people

parts.note: Hamlet was a prince of Denmark, so his people are Danes

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word Hamlet

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's prince is welcomed by one of his subjects, a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' puts P and H inside DANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne is a girl's name, also the nymph of Greek myth.

clue.text: Ship takes a gamble on the return journey

indicators.note: a return journey goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the football pools are a British betting game on match results

explanation.surface: A ship's passenger bets on the voyage home.
explanation.walkthrough: The pools are a British weekly bet on football results.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a one-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Hairs and airs sound like flairs

parts.note: putting on side means putting on airs, being pretentious
flairs sounds like flares, and flares are burns of fire

explanation.surface: A remark on pretension, flamboyance and hair.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDE is old British slang for swagger or airs; flairs heard aloud gives flares, which burn, so BURNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideburns are strips of hair grown down the sides of the face.

clue.text: Found her a crook without precedent

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or out of order, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman discovered a criminal acting in an unprecedented way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal noun; it is the Australian adjective for wrong or awry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never heard of before has no precedent at all.

clue.text: Mix up as Cairo becomes greedy

indicators.note: to mix things is to jumble them, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A muddle in Cairo makes someone grasping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix up' looks like one phrase, but 'up' belongs to the letters being mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacious means grasping and greedy, like a bird of prey.

clue.text: State taken in by a horsewoman in distress

indicators.note: the state's letters are held inside the following words

parts.note: a horse is a gee-gee, GG, and a woman is Eve
RI is Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: A US state is fooled by a rider who is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horsewoman' is one word but gives two pieces, horse and woman; gee-gee is British baby talk for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve someone is to wrong or upset them, so it is a verb meaning trouble or pain.

clue.text: Stop fellow becoming a cleaner

parts.note: to deter someone is to stop them acting
a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A man stops and takes a job as a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a cleaning agent such as washing powder.

clue.text: Go round organizing parties

indicators.note: organizing arranges things, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Doing the rounds while planning parties.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to trudge about from place to place.

clue.text: The time to write letters

definitions.meaning: a period, as in a ... of fine weather
to give the letters of a word in order

explanation.surface: The moment has come to write letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a period of time, and to spell is to set down a word's letters.

clue.text: Conveyance holds 50 less

indicators.note: the word for conveyance holds the numeral inside it

parts.note: a litter is a couch carried on poles to convey a person
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A vehicle carrying fifty is not big enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Littler is a comparative of little, meaning smaller or less in size.

clue.text: A collection of blood groups for this African native

parts.note: the blood groups are A, B, AB and O, so the letters B, A, O, B and AB are blood groups
the blood groups are A, B, AB and O, so the letters B, A, O, B and AB are blood groups

explanation.surface: A blood bank collects samples for an African.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A collection of' says several blood-group letters are gathered: B, A, O, B and AB.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is a huge-trunked tree native to Africa.

clue.text: White mark right on the jacket

parts.note: a blaze is a white stripe on a horse's face

explanation.surface: A white stain on the right side of a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazer is a smart, often striped or school, jacket.

clue.text: Want to mark the place

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
a city is a place where many people live

explanation.surface: A desire to deface a location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' looks like a verb; it is the noun meaning lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcity is a shortage, and want as a noun means lack.

clue.text: About the middle of April, old bailiff grants a respite

indicators.note: about means around, so the bailiff goes around the other letters

parts.note: a reeve was a medieval steward or bailiff

indicators.note: the middle of the word April is everything but its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A medieval bailiff gives a debtor time off in mid-April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' signals the container, the bailiff going round the middle of April; 'grants' only links, and the definition is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve is a temporary relief, a break from trouble.

clue.text: Get a form of protection by accepting official document

indicators.note: the word by takes the document inside it

parts.note: a roll is an official list or register

explanation.surface: Getting insurance by signing an official form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word, but it gives letters and is opened up by 'accepting'; 'Get' only introduces the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brolly is British slang for an umbrella, shelter from rain.

clue.text: Beetle initially seen by shelf

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word seen

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A beetle first spotted on a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' is not the insect but a heavy mallet, and a sledge is a sledgehammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is a heavy hammer, like a sledgehammer used for driving wedges.

clue.text: Tuberose 'development, I admit

indicators.note: a development reshapes something, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: A gardener concedes how a tuberose has grown.
explanation.walkthrough: A tuberose is a scented flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a conceding remark, like 'certainly' or 'admittedly'.
